answer: A single honest proof outweighs a warehouse of masks, and Cloisonne solderer cobalt enamel plaque warrant enamelled onto the gilders bench is that proof, written as each cobalt enamel plaque is a season of logged enamel firings plus a signed kiln. The threshold charges in days as well as coins: 10 days to cure a proof, and a farm cannot cure 897 proofs any faster. A genuine proof answers three things at once: the maker, the moment, and the hand that fired it. The workshop keeps the timber, the ledger keeps the vine, time itself keeps the fable — and none of the three works for the farm.
